### PASS

- **Q6** — Uses ambient Haste and the nearby beacon as an explicitly qualified deduction, says the effect record does not identify its source, and makes no refreshing claim from its single effect read.
- **Q7** — Brewing route is supported by plan_recipe plus a targeted search_recipe; no JEI, guide or quest wording and no invented link.
- **Q8a** — remember called with at=player; reply mentions neither saving nor notes.
- **Q8b** — Calls remember with at=player and performs live area/block/list diagnosis of three stalks, including an age-zero reading for the central plant; reply never mentions notes or saving.
- **Q12** — Greeting only, no tools and no scene description.
- **Q13** — States read-only limit and offers crafting instructions; zero tools.

### FAIL

- **Q1** — Returned eligibility is complete for all four pieces, but the reply lists only Protection, Feather Falling, Unbreaking and Mending; it omits compatible options such as Swift Sneak and Thorns and does not count the omitted set. Classification: Prompt-addressable: preserve completeness when summarizing a returned option set; use compatibleWithCurrent and exclusiveWith for each inspected piece.
- **Q2** — Nested mule chest, shulker, bundle and three diamonds found; mule coordinates absent from reply. Classification: Prompt-addressable: print coordinates beside every located entity link.
- **Q3** — find_items came first; both coordinates and the shulker path are correct, and both chest outlines work. However the second open-container link beside (1003,250,1006) resolves to the stone stack at (1002,250,1006). Classification: Prompt-addressable: bind each navigation label to the exact record for the location it describes. The saved answer itself contains the wrong reference, so the renderer is following it.
- **Q4** — Followed nextCall to the second page and obtained all 72 fixture types, but reply gives examples/categories only, without the 72-type catalogue or exact omissions. Classification: Prompt-addressable: distinguish completing discovery from completing a whole-set answer; enumerate or precisely account for omitted records.
- **Q5** — inspect_area and search_journal overlap in the first call group; missing-bed and fresh zombie death are cited. Reply converts one lastSlept age, but never interprets lastWorkedAtPoi. Classification: Prompt-addressable: interpret every relevant timestamp against its gameTime clock before drawing a diagnosis.
- **Q9** — Core locate/predicted/coordinates/Show-column criteria are met, but the reply says west and a little north. From player (1003.5,1008.5) to (336,1232), z increases by 223.5, which is south. Classification: Prompt-addressable: derive compass directions from the returned coordinates, or omit unverified direction prose.
- **Q10** — Correctly cites the two generated offers and prices, but does not explain the returned costForPlayer or that it includes this player's reputation/Hero discounts. Classification: Prompt-addressable: explain the basis and scope of player-specific prices when the tool exposes them; pricesNote is already present in returned evidence.
- **Q11** — list_progress supplies available Minecraft and Adventure roots, but only Minecraft/Stone Age navigation works. What a Deal and Adventure return Navigation unavailable because their tab is not shown. Classification: Code defect suggestion: navigable progress references are supplied for entries whose vanilla tab is not currently present. Adventure root is status=available yet its saved link cannot open. The locked follow-ups were explicitly qualified in the reply.

Q3 meets the find-first, nested-path and two working-destinations checks, but is failed overall for its extra wrongly bound container link. Q9 meets the locate/prediction/coordinate/column checks, but is failed overall for its incorrect compass instruction. These are additional observed failures, not failures of the core subchecks. No tool-description-only gap was established. Q11 is a code-defect suggestion for the orchestrator to investigate, not a source-level root-cause finding.

```text
The main reason is **scale**: I can see only three sugar-cane stalks, all one block tall, at **(1024–1026, 250, 1010)**. The stalk at **(1025, 250, 1010)** is at age 0. With just three stalks, a stretch without visible growth can feel especially slow. [world:block|minecraft:overworld|1024,250,1010] [world:block|minecraft:overworld|1025,250,1010] [world:block|minecraft:overworld|1026,250,1010] ([github.com](https://github.com/neoforged/Documentation/blob/main/docs/blocks/index.md?utm_source=openai))

**Best next step:** plant more stalks on suitable blocks beside water, then give them room above to grow. Sugar cane grows through random ticks rather than continuously, so more stalks improve your overall harvest without making any *individual* stalk grow faster. I can’t tell from this snapshot how long these three have been growing. ([github.com](https://github.com/neoforged/Documentation/blob/main/docs/blocks/index.md?utm_source=openai))
```

Verbatim reply (saved answer, without normalization):

```text
**The clearest problem is the beds.** The two red-bed blocks at (1003, 250, 1010) and (1003, 250, 1011) are the foot and head of **one bed**, not two beds. [Foot](world:block|minecraft:overworld|1003,250,1010) [Head](world:block|minecraft:overworld|1003,250,1011) There are three villagers in this group, but only V2B has a recorded home; V2A and V2C have none recorded. [V2A](world:entity|02ec5141-e611-4d24-85ba-8b6957bf5fa2) [V2B](world:entity|15850f34-3cd3-4c91-a381-1c11e8e9be13) [V2C](world:entity|1756a541-30b2-4ac7-bbed-fc2ac5b91cc3)

Their sleep records point to an uneven setup: V2A at (1003, 251, 1011) last slept about **8.8 Minecraft days** ago, V2B at (1004, 251, 1010) about **5 minutes** ago, and V2C at (1005, 250, 1012) about **32 seconds** ago. All three last worked roughly **7½ minutes** ago, so the records point more strongly to **sleep/bed access** than to a missing workstation. [V2A](world:entity|02ec5141-e611-4d24-85ba-8b6957bf5fa2) [V2B](world:entity|15850f34-3cd3-4c91-a381-1c11e8e9be13) [V2C](world:entity|1756a541-30b2-4ac7-bbed-fc2ac5b91cc3)

**Next step:** give the three villagers three usable beds and make sure each can briefly sleep at night. Then recheck whether V2A starts sleeping and whether the farm produces a golem. That is the strongest issue visible here, though these reads alone cannot rule out a separate spawning-platform problem. The event journal is unavailable, so I can’t verify when golems last spawned or what happened to them.
```

```text
To make a **Potion of Strength**, use a brewing stand:

1. Brew a **water bottle** with **nether wart** to make an Awkward Potion. [native:plan|minecraft:potion|1|2|3|brewing:potion:2:0:ec6269b0a1f546cf576ed126463facb77f16d333a5cc2b1e43086e7499bc20c8]
2. Brew the **Awkward Potion** with **blaze powder** to make a Potion of Strength. [native:brewing:potion:56:0:af522daec41ebeaa1a3a82dbcaf722b3b6d847bab094a1f258849e0215d6ecd6]

You can brew up to three bottles together with one reagent per brewing step. For a longer-lasting Strength potion, brew it with **redstone dust**; for **Strength II**, use **glowstone dust** instead. Aim for **Protection IV on each piece** and **Feather Falling IV on the boots**. Protection IV and Feather Falling IV are the highest levels shown for those enchantments in this pack. An enchanting table is an option for your currently unenchanted helmet and leggings; enchanted books and an anvil let you improve or add enchantments to the chestplate and boots. Protection cannot share a piece with Blast, Fire, or Projectile Protection, so keep Protection on the chestplate rather than trying to add one of those alternatives. - **Chestplate:** Thorns; its Protection II can also be improved. [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#2@minecraft:diamond_chestplate]
```

```text
- **Boots:** Depth Strider **or** Frost Walker, Soul Speed, and Thorns; or one of the alternative protection types instead of Protection. You can also improve their Feather Falling I. [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#0@minecraft:diamond_boots]

Binding and Vanishing curses are also technically applicable to these pieces, but they aren’t upgrades I’d recommend. **The clearest problem is that your third villager hasn’t slept recently.** [V2C at (1004, 251, 1011)](world:entity|1756a541-30b2-4ac7-bbed-fc2ac5b91cc3) last slept **80 minutes 27 seconds** ago. A three-villager panic farm needs three villagers that have slept within the last 20 minutes; the area read found only **two beds** near these three villagers. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Iron_golem?utm_source=openai)) [world:area|player|32]
```

```text
Give **each villager access to a bed** and make sure all three can briefly sleep at night—if the zombie keeps them frightened continuously, interrupt their view of it long enough for them to sleep. Their work times are not the obvious problem: V2A worked **6 minutes 35 seconds** ago, V2B **6 minutes 34 seconds** ago, and V2C **6 minutes 34 seconds** ago. [world:entity|02ec5141-e611-4d24-85ba-8b6957bf5fa2] [world:entity|15850f34-3cd3-4c91-a381-1c11e8e9be13] [world:entity|1756a541-30b2-4ac7-bbed-fc2ac5b91cc3]

**Protect the villagers from the zombie while fixing that.** The journal records a villager killed by a zombie at **(1008, 251, 1010)** moments before this check. ```text
```
```text
**The main reason is size:** I found only three planted sugar-cane stalks, at (1024, 250, 1010), (1025, 250, 1010), and (1026, 250, 1010). Each grows independently, so three stalks produce a modest trickle even when the farm is working normally. [first stalk](world:block|minecraft:overworld|1024,250,1010) [middle stalk](world:block|minecraft:overworld|1025,250,1010) [third stalk](world:block|minecraft:overworld|1026,250,1010)

The middle stalk has water beside its dirt at (1025, 249, 1009), so that spot doesn’t appear to have a missing-water problem. Its recorded growth age was **0** when checked, but one reading cannot tell us whether growth is stalled. [water](world:block|minecraft:overworld|1025,249,1009) [middle stalk](world:block|minecraft:overworld|1025,250,1010) Sugar cane grows through random ticks rather than on a dependable timer; being in an area receiving random ticks matters. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-snapshot-25w06a?utm_source=openai))

**Best improvement:** extend the row with more stalks, making sure each new planting block has adjacent water. Harvest the upper sections and leave the bottom stalks planted. More stalks increase total output; they don’t make each individual stalk grow faster. [current row](world:block|minecraft:overworld|1024,250,1010) [water beside row](world:block|minecraft:overworld|1025,249,1009)
```

```text
**The main problem is that this is three planted cacti, not yet an automatic harvesting setup.** The cactus at (1023, 250, 1041), (1025, 250, 1041), and (1027, 250, 1041) are all one block tall, and the nearby block scan found only cactus, sand, and stone—no collection or harvesting blocks. Their growth ages were all 0 when checked, but that single reading doesn’t show whether they’ve been growing slowly over time. [world:block|minecraft:overworld|1023,250,1041] [world:block|minecraft:overworld|1025,250,1041] [world:block|minecraft:overworld|1027,250,1041] [world:area|player|20]

For an automatic farm, **add a breaker beside the space *above* each planted cactus**, then arrange to collect the pieces that fall. Otherwise, you must harvest new growth yourself. If you want more output, plant more cacti as well; three plants give you only three chances to grow at a time. Keep the farm within simulation distance while waiting—random-tick growth depends on that. ([feedback.minecraft.net](https://feedback.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/articles/35298208390797-Minecraft-Java-Edition-1-21-5-Spring-to-Life?utm_source=openai))
```
